environment.scope: Archived native Android instrumentation in one API35 x86_64 KVM emulator using synthetic debug fixtures; no physical-device performance claim.

quantile_definition: Nearest rank ceil(p*n)-1, zero based; n=30 p50=sorted[14], p95=sorted[28], max=sorted[29]. Not the average of the two central samples.

duration_definitions.saveMs: (saveEndNs-saveStartNs)/1e6; repository-call and watchdog boundaries, with Committed and final content/revision verified. Not pure SQL writer wait or commit duration.
duration_definitions.firstCallTime: (collectorEndNs-collectorStartNs)/1e6; includes root/stat scan, guard checks and cleanup; overlaps author save in all 60 trials.
duration_definitions.finishCallTime: (finishEndNs-finishStartNs)/1e6; a separate collect after save and first collect finish.
duration_definitions.firstPlusFinishCallTime: Sum of the two GC call intervals, excluding the inter-call gap; never add overlapping save duration.
duration_definitions.firstStartToFinishEndTime: (finishEndNs-collectorStartNs)/1e6; includes inter-call gap, excludes fixture creation, final verification and cleanup.
duration_definitions.rootScans: after-roots callback count, one root-enumeration pass per collect; not all SELECT statements or source-body reads. These natural fixtures contain zero explicit roots.

exposure_definition: saveStartNs <= before-batch-commit timestamp <= saveEndNs. Hook is inside the GC writer transaction after actual DELETE statements of a nonempty batch and before commit. Point-in-call coverage, not lock-wait measurement. No such hook occurred in any first collect of methods 55/56.

correctness.verified_source_assertions: One root pass and one statistics pass across seven committed batches; 1280 sources and 257 previews deleted. Explicit Room refresh, actual observer notification, latest source retained, final audit reclaimableBytes=0.
Same Room author adds live root 300 after batch 1 commits: first deletes 256 then defers; follow-up deletes 1023; roots 300 and 1281 survive.
Separate Room author adds live root 300 after batch 1 commits: first deletes 256 then defers; follow-up deletes 1023; roots 300 and 1281 survive.

Same Room author starts while an actual 256-row DELETE transaction is held before commit. It cannot enter the held writer. After release, rename and new root 300 commit; subsequent GC guard defers. Follow-up deletes 1023; exact retained [300,1281], root snapshot and author revision/title/body verified.
correctness.timing_limit_note: 10s phase/gate waits and 2s post-release author await unchanged; deterministic correctness gates, not natural latency samples.

limits: Both groups are 0/30, below unchanged minimum 20. Exposed p50/p95/max remain null; all-save distributions are not actual-deletion-contention distributions.

All first calls scanned once, deleted zero and deferred; actual deletion of 1280 versions occurred only in each second call after save. Deferred means guard mismatch in this source path, but exact guard-vector deltas are not logged.
Methods 11/12 cover author requests queued behind actual DELETE work, commit/content and live-root safety under deterministic gates. Gate durations are not natural latency samples.

Each natural sample is a fresh 1281-source fixture and one rename. No high-root-cardinality, continuous writes, full-round concurrent deletion, fairness-under-sustained-writes or cross-version equivalence conclusion.
beforeRenameReceiptNs is inside the rename transaction, before its receipt; not transaction entry or physical commit timing.
Raw JUnit seconds and host/XML seconds describe whole-method windows, not per-save or deletion-only latency.
missing_evidence: At least 20 naturally exposed complete saves per connection mode under a prospectively frozen workload, retaining all outcomes.
Nonblocking writer transaction-entry and deletion batch/commit timing, or equivalent tracing, for a pure writer-queue/lock-hold claim.
Separately scoped common-source paired GC benchmark for a B-to-C1 GC or save regression conclusion.
minimal_next_step: Keep this result INSUFFICIENT_EXPOSURE and preserve workload, 30 trials, exposure rule, threshold and every sample. Do not substitute gated latencies or cherry-pick historical exposures.

Before additional execution, freeze one separately named diagnostic with nonblocking GC/author timeline recording and fixed stopping/sample rules. Existing after-scan, before-batch-commit, after-batch and BEFORE_RENAME_RECEIPT hooks localize scheduling; they cannot isolate full writer wait.

If a realistic additional workload is needed, define and label it separately before a future run. Do not change or relabel these samples, rerun until sufficient exposure, or bypass the conservative defer contract. No source edits or runs performed by this review.
